## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and the two prescribed families each have \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6, lines 14-42]
- [computed] For \((r,n-r,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\), with \(B=(6,6)\), the corrected truncated LR presentation has \(F\)-rank \(27\), \(106\) Pieri rows, and \(281\) LR rows. Both rational quotient-rank computations give \(2\). A selected Pieri sublattice has free columns \(e_{(1)},e_{(2)}\), global unimodular minor \(-1\), and contains every LR row integrally (`LR_rows_not_in_selected_Pieri_lattice = 0`). Its degree-block certificates \((\text{rows};\text{columns};\det)\) are  
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
  2&(1;1)&11&1\\
  3&(1;11),(1;2)&21,3&1\\
  4&(1;21),(1;3),(2;11)&22,31,4&-1\\
  5&(1;22),(1;31),(1;4)&32,41,5&1\\
  6&(1;32),(1;41),(1;5),(2;22)&33,42,51,6&1\\
  7&(1;33),(1;42),(1;51)&43,52,61&1\\
  8&(1;43),(1;52),(1;61)&44,53,62&1\\
  9&(1;44),(1;53)&54,63&1\\
  10&(1;54),(1;63)&55,64&1\\
  11&(1;55)&65&1\\
  12&(1;65)&66&1
  \end{array}
  \]
  Here \((\lambda;\mu)\) denotes the row for \(s_\lambda s_\mu\), and strings denote partitions. [artifact 27afdb63404a159fb655ddde4867d0e60d06159e2e64e4f8523604222057256a]
- [computed] For \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), with \(B=(2,2,2,2,2)\), the corrected truncated LR presentation has \(F\)-rank \(20\), \(33\) Pieri rows, and \(155\) LR rows. Both rational quotient-rank computations give \(2\). A selected Pieri sublattice has free columns \(e_{(1)},e_{(2)}\), global unimodular minor \(-1\), and contains every LR row integrally. Its degree-block certificates are  
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
  2&(1;1)&11&1\\
  3&(1;11),(1;2)&111,21&1\\
  4&(1;111),(1;21),(2;11)&1111,211,22&-1\\
  5&(1;1111),(1;211),(1;22)&11111,2111,221&1\\
  6&(1;11111),(1;2111),(1;221)&21111,2211,222&1\\
  7&(1;21111),(1;2211)&22111,2221&1\\
  8&(1;22111),(1;2221)&22211,2222&1\\
  9&(1;22211)&22221&1\\

  [artifact 27afdb63404a159fb655ddde4867d0e60d06159e2e64e4f8523604222057256a]
- [proved] In both cases, the LR relation lattice equals the selected Pieri lattice: selected Pieri rows are LR rows, while the exact containment test gives the reverse inclusion. The unimodular block minor makes this lattice a graph over all columns except \(e_{(1)},e_{(2)}\). Therefore
  \[
  J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z e_{(1)}\oplus\mathbb Z e_{(2)}\cong\mathbb Z^2.
  \]
  Equivalently, the Smith forms are \(\operatorname{diag}(1^{25},0^2)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(1^{18},0^2)\), respectively.
- [proved] Here \(a=b=1\), so the two prescribed families are \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\). The first maps to the displayed basis of the quotient; the degree-\(2\) Pieri relation is \(e_{(2)}+e_{(1,1)}=0\), so the second does also. Hence neither family admits deletion while still generating \(J_v\).

## Strategy
Use columns indexed by \(\mu\) with \((1)\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\). Form all truncated LR multiplication rows, independently form the Pieri submatrix, and certify equality of their integral row lattices by membership in a saturated unimodular Pieri sublattice.

## Gaps
The computation proves only these two finite parameter cases; it does not establish a uniform Smith-form formula.
